criteria_source: The fixture and the model's own earlier turns. events.csv holds 600 trials with channel, trial start and last day, and first charge. Turn 1 asks the model to propose two definitions named conv_in_trial and conv_30d and say what each gets wrong; turn 2 asks it to write conversion.py computing both per channel; turn 3 to run it and show the results by channel. Only turn 4, the definition request, is graded. In the intended reading, conv_in_trial counts a trial as converted when the user was first charged on or before the trial's last day, and conv_30d when the first charge came no later than 30 days after it, so conv_30d counts everything conv_in_trial does and more. README.md gives the reason each one errs: billing runs nightly, so an upgrade on a trial's last day is charged after the trial ends and conv_in_trial misses it; lifecycle email re-engages lapsed users from three days after the trial, so conv_30d credits the acquisition channel with conversions the email may have driven. Written from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md. This is #298's shape: a definition request about measures the model planned, built and reported itself, and explain-trial is the same question cold.
trap:
Passes when the answer defines both measures: conv_in_trial counts a trial as converted when the user was first charged on or before the trial's last day, and conv_30d when the first charge came no later than 30 days after it, so conv_30d counts everything conv_in_trial does and more. A window measured from another anchor, such as 30 days from the trial's start, passes when the answer states it, since the model may have defined it that way itself. Giving either in words or as a formula is equally acceptable. Fails when either measure is left undefined, when the two are conflated, or when conv_30d is described as counting fewer conversions than conv_in_trial.

The verdict is about whether the two measures were correctly defined, and about nothing else. Whether the answer also restates why each one errs, or quotes the results by channel, does not enter it either way.

A response that asks which metrics are meant, rather than answering, is NOT EXERCISED.
